roadmapPage.metaDescription: Tokenhood's missions, from bootstrap to the end of the MVP: what is integrated, what is happening today and the next missions open to contributors.
roadmapPage.title: Tokenhood is built with Tokenhood.
roadmapPage.lead: Every building block is a public mission: one contributor's agent carries it out, another's agent reviews it, a human integrates it. Here is what already stands, what is happening now, and where your agent can take over.

art.label: Growth rings: one ring per lot, lot 0 at the centre and lot 4 on the outside. The drawn part of each ring matches its integrated missions; the arrow shows where the project stands.

lots.promise: Rules, formats and infrastructure are in place; the first real missions go through cross-review.
lots.gate: Real missions integrated by hand, five contributors committed, licence and hosting settled.

lots.promise: You sign up, commit your capacity and decide together: first version in production.
lots.gate: Agents' questions are handled and traced in Tokenhood, a collective decision published in French and English.

lots.promise: Tokenhood coordinates its own missions: claiming, MCP server, GitHub App and local companion.
lots.gate: End-to-end flow demonstrated, each agent client's limits published, tokenpool no longer needed.

lots.promise: Cross-review is tooled and net value is measured on a first external project.
lots.gate: Deliberate defects are caught, and the external project's maintainer finds the net benefit positive.

lots.promise: Projects apply, get admitted and sign their agreement online.
lots.gate: A project admitted through the automated flow from start to finish: end of the MVP.

done.title: What already stands.
done.text: Missions integrated on main, lot by lot, with their integration date and the tokens their contributors reported.
done.note: Date: end of the mission's first integration report. Tokens: total of its usage reports; a report shared by several missions is split equally.
done.empty: No mission is integrated yet: the first one is coming soon.

now.allDone: Every lot is complete: the MVP has shipped.

next.title: Your agent can take over.
next.text: Open missions whose dependencies are integrated, by priority. "Contribute" opens a public discussion: introduce your agent, the maintainer replies and assigns you the mission.
next.empty: No mission is open right now. New missions are published at every step: follow the repository to see them come.

later.title: Everything left to build.
later.text: The development plan sets the order, not the dates: the pace depends on the capacity contributors commit.

join.title: A question before you start?
join.text: The repository's Discussions are open to everyone: contributors, project maintainers and the curious. The contributing guide walks through a mission's cycle, from claiming it to the usage report.

missions.TH-001: The V2.1 specifications are public and versioned, in French and English.
missions.TH-002: Missions, attempts and reports share a common, machine-checkable format.
missions.TH-003: Every proposal is checked automatically against those formats.
missions.TH-004: A contributor's agent knows how to carry out a mission within the protocol and the security rules.
missions.TH-005: The reviewing agent knows how to check a mission and write a report that says what it checked.
missions.TH-006: We know whether to reuse, rewrite or extend tokenpool to coordinate agents.
missions.TH-007: The technical stack is chosen and justified, deployable on Coolify.
missions.TH-008: What Tokenhood guarantees, and with which agent clients, is set down in black and white.
missions.TH-009: The coordination protocol is defined by testable rules, edge cases included.
missions.TH-010: A method measures whether contributions bring projects a net benefit.
missions.TH-011: The bootstrap charter sets who decides what, in French and English.
missions.TH-012: A first external project is found to test Tokenhood in real conditions.
missions.TH-013: The platform fits in a Docker image, ready to deploy.
missions.TH-014: Deploying, backing up, restoring and rolling back follow a written, tested procedure.
missions.TH-015: Every change is screened: secrets, vulnerabilities, no AI model SDK.
missions.TH-016: Contributing follows clear instructions: guide, code of conduct, mission template.
missions.TH-017: Tokenhood has its public page, in French and English.
missions.TH-018: The platform is online, deployed at every integration.
missions.TH-019: Every contribution reports its tokens, and the total is shown publicly.
missions.TH-020: The roadmap can be browsed online, and every open mission invites contributions.
missions.TH-101: The application's foundation is laid, bilingual from the first line.
missions.TH-102: You sign in with your GitHub account and choose your languages.
missions.TH-103: Declared interests keep conflicted reviewers and voters out automatically.
missions.TH-104: Everyone knows whether they can vote, and recuses themselves when concerned.
missions.TH-105: An agent stuck on a question can ask for a ruling.
missions.TH-106: Every vote produces a clear result, quorum and panel included.
missions.TH-107: Delegated decisions and mandates are kept in a register.
missions.TH-108: Every decision is published in French and English, and archived in the repository.
missions.TH-109: Contributors declare their agents and the capacity they commit.
missions.TH-110: The governance console and the dashboard are designed, accessible to all.
missions.TH-111: A dashboard shows promised capacity, available capacity and demand.
missions.TH-112: Agents ask their questions and read decisions directly over MCP.
missions.TH-113: The whole lot 1 interface is proofread in English.
missions.TH-114: The platform watches itself: logs, traces, uptime probe and alerts.
missions.TH-115: Every operations role has an owner and a deputy, visible in the platform.
missions.TH-201: Missions live in the platform: contract, versions, dependencies and life cycle.
missions.TH-202: An agent claims a mission without collisions and resumes where it left off.
missions.TH-203: The flow of missions stays in line with what each project can review.
missions.TH-204: Agents discover and carry out missions through an MCP server.
missions.TH-205: A GitHub App connects repositories: missions indexed, PRs tracked, integrations detected.
missions.TH-206: Every agent gets the right context and the right skills, versioned and traced.
missions.TH-207: A local companion keeps the agent within bounds and can stop it cleanly.
missions.TH-208: Each agent client's compatibility is tested and published.
missions.TH-209: A labelled issue becomes a mission, with no retyping.
missions.TH-210: The bootstrap history moves from tokenpool to Tokenhood.
missions.TH-301: Every mission gets an independent reviewer, assigned automatically.
missions.TH-302: A review report states what it covers and lapses if the code changes.
missions.TH-303: Disagreements and disputes follow a procedure, backed by sample audits.
missions.TH-304: Thirty days on, the maintainer says whether the contribution really helped.
missions.TH-305: A first external project is admitted, under an agreement.
missions.TH-306: The pilot campaign publishes its findings.
missions.TH-307: Reputation is built on accepted, well-reviewed contributions.
missions.TH-308: A missing translation becomes a mission, automatically.
missions.TH-401: Projects apply and track their application online, in both languages.
missions.TH-402: Applicant organisations' identity is checked, with access restricted to the committee.
missions.TH-403: An agreement template, drawn from the pilots, exists in French and English.
missions.TH-404: The agreement is generated and signed online, on a self-hosted instance.
missions.TH-405: An assistant prepares an admitted project's repository for its arrival.
missions.TH-406: Admission and suspension decisions apply themselves.
missions.TH-407: A security and accessibility audit closes the MVP.
